transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jason Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Verdant CTO), Priya Menon (Verdant Lead ML Eng), Sophie Li (Product), Ethan Rogers (Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on rapid onramp using Redwood hosted API, tradeoffs vs Dedicated/Private, security and data-residency constraints, and a proposed 2-week pilot to validate latency and cost. Customer is PLG-first — wants self-serve credits but enterprise guardrails; main concerns: latency tail, KMS integration, audit logs, and ability to fall back to smaller quantized variants to save cost.

Topics covered:
- Time-to-first-request / time-to-first-inference for PLG flow
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- Pilot plan: 100k tokens/day benchmark, latency P95 targets, cost estimates
- Integration: SDKs, streaming, function/tool calling, and telemetry hooks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jason: hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, i'm Jason from Redwood, AE on this account, i'll run through goals then hand over to Maya for tech.
[00:10] Liam: thanks Jason, quick background — Verdant does realtime summarization for analyst dashboards, low latency matters for our UX, also we have regulatory customers in eu so residency matters.
[00:20] Maya: cool, quick clarifying q, is the primary ask self-serve quickstart with free credits and then escalate to a pilot for production?
[00:26] Sophie: yeah that sums it up; product wants to see a demo flow within a day or two and then a 2-week pilot to validate.
[00:33] Jason: perfect. we'll cover hosted quickstart - how fast you can get to first request, then the Dedicated & Private options 
[00:41] Maya: also i'll flag where infra knobs live — batching, kv cache (transcribed sometimes as K V cash), and fallback model variants.

[01:15] Ethan: just to flag infra constraints — we run in a eu-west region, EKM for keys, and we need outbound egress rules locked down.
[01:25] Jason: understood. Redwood Hosted supports region pinning and we have private deployment options too; for hosted you can restrict region to eu-west and we support bring-your-own-KMS via our enterprise plan — that's the Dedicated/Private path.
[01:40] Priya: what is the approx time to first request if we go self-serve? we want to get a developer to generate a summary in under 30 minutes ideally.
[01:47] Maya: with the PLG credits / quickstart it's typically under 20 minutes: sign up, API key, SDK snippet, run a few sample calls. time-to-first-token usually measured in minutes — the only delay is onboarding and token-provisioning.
[02:02] Liam: ok. but we're worried about tail latency on long docs; also cost if we have many small requests.
[02:10] Maya: right — our runtime does continuous batching and prefix caching which helps with micro-requests; for long docs you can do chunking or streaming generation. if you need strict p95 targets we recommend Dedicated where you get reserved capacity and better guaranteed tails.
[02:25] Sophie: can you quantify that? like p95 numbers on a 32k context model?
[02:31] Maya: rough ballpark on 32k for hosted varies by load; in our benchmarks a typical p95 is 220-320ms for standard prompt sizes, for sustained high concurrency Dedicated can get you down to 120-180ms depending on instance type and batching config. those are ballpark; we can run a short benchmark as part of the pilot to measure on your workload.
[02:52] Ethan: and what about cost difference? we don't want to overcommit.
[02:56] Jason: hosted is usage-based and great for PLG/evaluations; Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) that drives unit-cost down. our Optimize tool will recommend batching/quantization to hit cost targets. we can put numbers in the pricing sheet.

[04:10] (short crosstalk)
[04:30] Priya: on security: SOC2 is required, we also need detailed audit logs, SAML SSO for dev users, and BYOK/KMS. how mature are those features?
[04:41] Jason: we are SOC2 Type II; we have audit logs, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and enterprise plans support BYOK via KMS or HSM integration in Dedicated/Private. i'll attach our security pack link in follow-up.
[04:55] Sophie: can logs be pushed to our SIEM?
[05:00] Maya: yes we have forwarding hooks and can stream logs to your SIEM or to a secure S3. also per-request metadata and token-level cost tracing are available in the console.

[06:15] Liam: for PII, do you redact at rest or does customer control retention?
[06:22] Jason: by default hosted retains minimal logs for billing and debugging but enterprise configs allow zero retention; for Private deployments you control retention entirely. we'll include options in the security doc.

[07:00] Priya: for the pilot we want to test both accuracy regressions and latency/cost, can Redwood run evals against a fixed prompt set?
[07:07] Maya: yes, our Optimize stack can run evals and regression alerts. typical pilot: 2 weeks, run 10k annotated prompts from your corpus, collect generation quality metrics and latency/cost. we feed results into rollout policies.
[07:23] Sophie: that sounds good. what's the onboarding flow for engineers?
[07:28] Jason: sign up, claim PLG credits, we provide a quickstart repo. Maya will do a 45-minute hands-on session for Priya/Ethan.
[07:36] (brief pause)
[07:50] Ethan: small nit — can we run the SDK in our air-gapped staging?
[07:55] Maya: for air-gapped you move to Private on-prem package; we ship an appliance and there's a private control plane option. that's more involved but supported, and we can scope that if required.

[09:20] (discussion of fallback)
[09:35] Priya: another question — we sometimes need deterministic generations for some flows, how do you support that?
[09:40] Maya: you can pin model versions and use temperature/seed controls. for deterministic we recommend lower temp and fixed seed; we also preserve KV cache behavior across sessions for consistency.
[09:50] Liam: can we do canary rollouts?
[09:53] Maya: yes — Redwood Console supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback to stable variants if quality regressions are detected.

[12:10] Sophie: are there any limitations on file size or number of tokens in a single request?
[12:16] Maya: depends on model/context length — some models support 8k/32k/64k contexts. for very large files recommended chunking + retrieval augmented generation.

[15:30] (customer asks about real customer examples)
[15:35] Jason: we've done similar pilots with fintech and health analytics where they started PLG, used hosted for the POC, then moved to Dedicated as throughput grew. i'll share two one-page case studies.

[17:05] Priya: ok pilot plan specifics?
[17:08] Maya: propose: 2-week pilot, 100k tokens/day target, measure p95 latency < 300ms on representative prompts, quality evaluation on 10k prompts. we provide a benchmark script and can run joint runs in your eu region.
[17:25] Liam: budget wise do you have a ballpark? we prefer not to buy Dedicated up-front.
[17:30] Jason: you can run the pilot on hosted with PLG credits; if results show need for Dedicated, we can size reserved capacity and show monthly commit numbers. i'll send Hosted vs Dedicated cost sheet.

[20:00] (silence, note taking)
[20:20] Sophie: sounds like next steps are clear, can we get the documentation links?
[20:25] Jason: sure — i'll send: hosted quickstart repo link, security pack (SOC2 + KMS guide), pricing sheet, and a proposed pilot SOW.
[20:34] Maya: i'll follow up with the benchmark script and suggested model/config for test.
[20:39] Priya: and we'll confirm stakeholders and test data set by Jan 14th.

[22:10] (wrap-up)
[22:15] Jason: recap: 1) Jason sends pricing + security docs + quickstart links, 2) Maya sends pilot benchmark plan and script, 3) Verdant confirms residency and stakeholders. aim to kick off week of Jan 19.
[22:33] Liam: great thanks everyone.
[22:36] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cash'); filler words left in to preserve authenticity. Links referenced during call: quickstart repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/verdant), security pack (link omitted in transcript, will be sent in follow-up), pricing spreadsheet (drive link to be emailed).
